An sRGB colour. Grayscale devices use its luminance.

One entry of a directory listing.
Everything the core needs to know about a screen.

Input hardware a device offers.
An input event reported by a shell.

A point in time in milliseconds on a monotonic clock with an arbitrary
origin (e.g. boot). Only differences are meaningful.
Vertical metrics of a font at a size, in pixels.

How much memory the device has for PaperPaw. Everything must work
with [`MemoryClass::Small`]; on large devices plugins may use more to
be faster or show more (caches, covers in lists), never to work at all.
Storage for devices without any: everything is empty and read-only.
The memory layout of a framebuffer.
A point in logical screen coordinates.
A single pointer sample in logical screen coordinates.
Phase of a pointer (finger, pen, mouse) interaction.
What touches the screen.
An axis-aligned rectangle of screen pixels.
E-ink refresh modes, from slowest/cleanest to fastest/dirtiest.
Storage provided by a shell.
Why a storage operation failed.

The shell's view of time and power. Unknown parts are `None`: a desktop
has no battery, a device without a clock chip no time of day.

Looks up messages in all loaded catalogs, following the fallback chain of
the selected language.

Wall-clock time: at the monotonic time `at`, it was `unix_millis`
milliseconds since 1970 (UTC). Later times follow from the monotonic
clock, so shells report it once and again only when it is corrected.
An annotation with what is shown of it.
Where an annotation is.

doc: Passes `value` along: it comes back in the answer's context.

Asks to choose one of a few options, under `title` (already
translated); the option chosen comes as `reply`, nothing when the
reader goes back. Asked on the screen of slot
[`CHOICE`](crate::builtin::slots::CHOICE):

Asks yes or no, with `question` (already translated) as the title; the
answer comes as `reply`, a [`Confirmed`], nothing when the reader goes
back or taps outside. The buttons say *Yes* and *No* unless given
words of their own; the focus starts on no, the safe answer, unless
[`focus_yes`](ConfirmQuestion::focus_yes). Asked on the screen of slot
[`CONFIRM`](crate::builtin::slots::CONFIRM):
Asks for a folder; the answer comes as `reply`.

Asks for text, under `title` (already translated); the answer comes as
`reply`.

What an icon says rather than which it is: drawn with the icon a
plugin names for it ([`Registrar::add_icon`](crate::Registrar::add_icon),
e.g. `r.add_icon(icons::BACK, "arrow-big-left".into())`), else with
its default ([`default_of`]), else as PaperPaw draws it itself (the
arrows of headers and the keyboard's keys).

Removes what plugins kept for books no longer on the storage
([`Registrar::add_book_data`](crate::Registrar::add_book_data)),
e.g. deleted from a computer.

Asks yes or no, e.g. whether to delete a book (a box in the middle
of the screen): asked with [`ask::confirm`](crate::ask::confirm),
answered with a [`Confirmed`](crate::replies::Confirmed), nothing
on *Back* or a tap outside. Every plugin's yes or no questions come
here, so a screen bound here asks them all another way (see
[`ui::confirm`](crate::ui::confirm) for its parameters).

The start screen. The default is a dashboard, but any screen can be
bound here: a file browser, a bookshelf, a single "continue" button.
Opens the library slot.

Select held: what a long press does where the focus is, where a
screen takes it (a widget's own, see
[`WidgetTarget::hold`](crate::widgets::WidgetTarget::hold)); else
the menu, as before.

Shows a menu (an overlay). Opened with the parameter
[`MENU`](super::params::MENU).

"Forward" in the widest sense: next list entry, increase a value
being edited; screens without such a meaning treat it as the next
page. Lets devices with very few buttons operate everything.

Does nothing: bound to an input, it stops the input from doing
anything there.

*Open with…* in the book menu ([`menus::BOOK`](super::menus::BOOK)):
asks which reading app opens the book this time
([`readers::ask_once`](crate::readers::ask_once)).
The opposite of [`NEXT`].

Opens the quick panel from the top of the screen: the menu
[`QUICK`](super::menus::QUICK) as a panel of controls (night mode,
light, turning the screen, …). A swipe down from the top edge
opens it.

Refreshes the whole screen with a flash, clearing what e-ink left
of earlier pictures (ghosting).

Saves what the screen shows as a picture, in `Screenshots` beside
the library ([`Command::Screenshot`](crate::Command::Screenshot)).
Opens the settings slot.

Puts the device to sleep: shows the sleep screen (slot
[`SLEEP`](super::slots::SLEEP)), then the shell sleeps until it is
woken (see [`Capabilities::sleep`](crate::Capabilities)). Where the system sleeps on
its own (Android), nothing sends it.
Opens the tools menu ([`menus::TOOLS`](super::menus::TOOLS)).
The book whose annotations changed ([`ANNOTATIONS_CHANGED`]).
A book that came into the library ([`BOOK_ADDED`]).
What changed of a book ([`BOOK_CHANGED`]).

An action was chosen for a book in the library
([`BOOK_CHOSEN`], [`menus::BOOK`](super::menus::BOOK)).
A book that was moved or renamed ([`BOOK_MOVED`]).
A book that was deleted ([`BOOK_REMOVED`]).
The catalog wanted ([`CATALOG_WANTED`]).

A decorated word that was tapped, or chosen with the buttons
([`DECORATION_TAPPED`]): the decorator's mark it is in.

doc:
The bookmarks or highlights of a book changed
([`annotations`](crate::annotations), [`AnnotationsChanged`]).
Readers show them anew, syncs pass them on.

The battery was measured again ([`Env::status`](crate::Env::status)),
about once a minute where the device measures it: for plugins that
record its use. Nothing need be drawn anew.

A book came into the library ([`BookAdded`]): received, downloaded,
copied by a plugin. Whoever brings a book emits it
([`library::added`](crate::library::added)); views may show it at
once, the catalog is made anew.

Something of a book changed ([`BookChanged`]): its details, how far
it is read, its cover, whether it is a favourite, a plugin's field.
Sent by the kernel for the reading events and by plugins that change
a book ([`library::changed_book`](crate::library::changed_book));
views show the book anew.

An action of the book menu ([`menus::BOOK`](super::menus::BOOK)) was
chosen for a book ([`BookChosen`]), sent just before it runs: the
plugin whose action it is does it for that book.

The book read was closed (the reader left, or another book
opened): where it was left ([`Reading`]).

The last page of a book was reached, once each time it is opened
([`Reading`]).

A book file was moved or renamed ([`BookMoved`]). Plugins that keep
data by a book's path move it along (progress, notes, statistics).

A book was opened for reading ([`Reading`]). Every reader plugin
emits it, so home screens, statistics or sync plugins work with any
reader. Not for documents in hidden folders
([`files::is_hidden`](crate::files::is_hidden)), e.g. web pages:
they are no books.

A book file was deleted ([`BookRemoved`]): what plugins keep for it
goes ([`Registrar::add_book_data`](crate::Registrar::add_book_data)
folders by the kernel; other data by the plugin). Whoever deletes a
book emits it.

The catalog of the library was made anew
([`library::catalog`](crate::library::catalog)): views of it read it
again.

The catalog is wanted ([`CatalogWanted`],
[`library::request_catalog`](crate::library::request_catalog)):
the kernel walks the library in the background where needed.

A word a decorator marked was tapped, or chosen with the buttons
([`DecorationTapped`]); sent for decorators that take taps (see
[`decorations`](crate::decorations)), whose plugin answers.

A document that a format could not open yet
([`DocumentError::NotReady`](crate::document::DocumentError), e.g.
still coming in) is there now ([`DocumentReady`]): its format's
plugin says so, readers waiting for it open it.

An install of a firmware update went on, ended or failed
([`Firmware::state`](crate::firmware::Firmware), see
[`firmware`](crate::firmware)).

The focus of the buttons moved to another part of the screen
([`FocusChanged`]): for screen readers of one's own. Worked out
only while a plugin listens or the focus is spoken.

A link of the open book is to be followed ([`FollowLink`]), as a
tap on it would: the reader goes there (or opens a web address in
the browser). A footnote shown over the page sends it to go to the
note.

Books came into the library or left it (received, downloaded,
copied, deleted): views of the library read it again. Plugins that
change the library emit it ([`library::changed`](crate::library::changed));
a move is [`BOOK_MOVED`].

A lookup provider that answered later ([`LookupAnswered`], see
[`lookup`](crate::lookup)) has its entry, for a query that names
no reply of its own (`LookupQuery::reply`): the screen that asked
shows it.
A menu was redefined or reset ([`MenuChanged`]).

Nothing uses the network any more (no request, server or
connection), where PaperPaw manages Wi-Fi: e.g. to switch the radio
off a little later.

A plugin's request, server or connection waits for the network,
where PaperPaw manages Wi-Fi and is in none: e.g. to join one.

A book's notes were exported as a file ([`NotesExported`]), for
plugins that take them further (a notes app, a sync). Readers send
it; its form is Markdown.

The room of a page layer was tapped, or chosen with the buttons
([`PageLayerTapped`]); sent for layers that take taps (see
[`layers`](crate::layers)), whose plugin answers.
The reader moved to another page ([`Reading`]).

The words of the page shown are wanted ([`PageWordsWanted`]):
a reader with a book open answers with
[`reading::PageWords`](crate::reading::PageWords).

A data plugin was loaded or removed while running
([`Command::LoadPlugin`](crate::Command::LoadPlugin),
[`Command::RemovePlugin`](crate::Command::RemovePlugin)): lists of
plugins, fonts and presets read them anew.

The power level or mode changed ([`power`](crate::power)), e.g. by
the battery in Automatic.

The values shown without being kept changed, or ended (see
[`Command::PreviewSettings`](crate::Command::PreviewSettings)).

The reading app of a book or a folder is to be chosen
([`ReadingAppWanted`]): the kernel lists the readers that fit.

How long was read today ([`ReadToday`]), as the plugin that keeps
the reading statistics counts it (`stats`): sent as it records
reading, as it starts and as the device learns the date, when the
number changed. Plugins that show it (a reading goal) keep the
last one: on a day after its `day`, nothing was read yet.
Back from [`SUSPEND`].

Another screen is shown on top ([`ScreenShown`]): one opened, or
the one below a screen closed. The whole stack is in
[`Env::stack`](crate::Env::stack). For plugins that subscribe:
screens learn that they show from [`Screen::on_show`](crate::Screen::on_show).
After a setting changed: which ([`SettingChanged`]).

Text typed for a setting, asked with its parameter
[`ID`](super::params::ID) (as [`ui::setting_opens`](crate::ui::setting_opens)
asks): the kernel sets the setting to it, trimmed.

Skimming through the book being read (an overlay): opened with the
parameters of [`events::Skimmed`](super::events::Skimmed) (where the
book is, where its chapters begin). It asks the reader to move with
[`events::SKIM`](super::events::SKIM) and hears where the book is
then with [`events::SKIMMED`](super::events::SKIMMED).

Where the book being skimmed is now ([`Skimmed`]): the reader tells
the skimming overlay after each move.

After the home screen has been opened at start-up. Plugins use it to
e.g. reopen the last book.
The battery or the time zone changed; status lines redraw.

PaperPaw stops (the device restarts, or an app closes for good):
save what is pending, as at [`SUSPEND`]; the device may lose its
power right after. No [`RESUME`] follows, and it is no sleep.

The device goes to sleep or the app to the background: a moment to
save or send what is pending.

An action was chosen for text chosen in a book ([`TextChosen`]),
just before it runs: the plugin whose action it is reacts (e.g. a
"Share" action needs no more than a menu entry in
[`menus::SELECTION`](super::menus::SELECTION) and this event).

What a widget shows changed by other means than the events screens
already follow, e.g. a tap on it turned to another quote or ticked
an item off ([`WidgetChanged`]): screens showing it read it anew
([`Widget::update`](crate::widgets::Widget::update)). See
[`widgets::changed`](crate::widgets::changed).

The Wi-Fi state changed ([`Env::wifi`](crate::Env), see
[`wifi`](crate::wifi)).
Joining a network failed ([`WifiFailed`]).
Networks were found ([`Wifi::networks`](crate::wifi::Wifi)).
A word of a book was looked up ([`WordLookedUp`]).

What held work or requests back no longer does (the mode changed,
the reader switched a plugin's network on, went online): a plugin
told [`Retry::WhenAllowed`](crate::work::Retry::WhenAllowed) may
try again.

A plugin's declared work changed its state or its progress (at most
once a second), sent to that plugin, e.g. for its page; the work's
id comes as [`params::ID`](super::params::ID).

A plugin's declared work was taken out because it can never run
(its network switched off, not declared in its manifest), sent to
that plugin; work only held back stays queued (see
[`work`](crate::work)).

Icons (see [`icons`](crate::icons)); without a font here, menus
show text only.
Book text: font size, spacing, hyphenation, …
Bold book text; readers fall back to [`READING`] without it.
Bold italic book text; readers fall back to [`READING_BOLD`].
Italic book text; readers fall back to [`READING`] without it.

The status lines while reading: as the menus ([`UI`]), as the book
([`READING`]) or a family of their own, as
[`settings::STATUS_FONT`](super::settings::STATUS_FONT) says.
Readers draw their status lines in it.
Menus, labels and other user interface text.
Buttons and gestures.

Developer options: the settings of
[`groups::DEVELOPER`](super::groups::DEVELOPER) show, and plugins may
show what only developers need (e.g. what each plugin took).
Screen: night mode, menu size, refresh.
Opens the library slot.

How menus and lists look: text size, margins, rows, lines, headers.
Themes (data plugins) set its defaults.

Marks in the text: the looks of the roles of decorations (see
[`decorations`](crate::decorations)), a section per role.
Settings whose plugin names no registered group.
Book text: font size, spacing, hyphenation, …
Chooses the status lines a setting lists.
Language and everything about the device.

Taps on the left turn forward, on the right back: for the left
hand.
No preset: the plugins' default bindings.
[`STANDARD`] as a static string, e.g. for setting values.

Everything with "forward" and "back": short press moves, long press
on forward confirms (opens the menu while reading), long press on
back goes back.

What there is to open besides the tools: a plugin's own app (a
game, a notebook). What a launcher, a drawer or a palette lists:
these and the [`TOOLS`]; the shipped home screen's grid of tools
shows both.

What can be done with a book, wherever a library lists it (its
sheet: open, finished, favourite, information, …): plugins add
their actions (send it, sync it now, delete it); when one is
chosen, the library sends [`events::BOOK_CHOSEN`](super::events::BOOK_CHOSEN)
with the book, then runs it.

The menu shown when a screen has no menu of its own: short and
always the same (home, library, tools, night mode, settings).

*Open with…* in the book menu ([`menus::BOOK`](super::menus::BOOK)):
asks which reading app opens the book this time
([`readers::ask_once`](crate::readers::ask_once)).

The quick panel ([`actions::QUICK_PANEL`](super::actions::QUICK_PANEL)):
switches and controls for quick changes, from every plugin.
Shows a book. Opened with the parameter [`PATH`](super::params::PATH).

The reader's submenu "More": what is used less often (statistics,
syncing a book, profiles).

The reader's panel of font and layout, shown over the page; plugins
add controls such as the light.

What can be done with text chosen in a book (look it up, share,
translate): plugins add their actions; when one is chosen, the
reader sends [`events::TEXT_CHOSEN`](super::events::TEXT_CHOSEN),
then runs it.
Opens the settings slot.
Opens the tools menu ([`menus::TOOLS`](super::menus::TOOLS)).
An action to run, e.g. when the title of a menu bar is tapped.

What a screen shows focused first, e.g. a setting in
[`slots::SETTINGS`](super::slots::SETTINGS).

Where something was before, e.g. a moved book
([`events::BOOK_MOVED`](super::events::BOOK_MOVED)).

Entries a menu leaves out this time, as ids separated by commas:
what does not apply where it is opened (e.g. searching a comic).
An id, e.g. of the setting in `core.setting-changed`.
A BCP 47 language tag, e.g. of the book a word is from.

Set (to `1`) when a question is answered on each change too, e.g.
the keyboard's ([`ask::TextQuestion::live`](crate::ask::TextQuestion::live)).

Shows a menu (an overlay). Opened with the parameter
[`MENU`](super::params::MENU).

What kind of text a keyboard asks for: `text` (the default),
`number` or `password` (shown as dots).

The page (from 1) and the number of pages, once a reader has
counted them.
A storage path, e.g. of the book to open.
Reading progress in percent, e.g. `12.5`.

Why something failed, e.g. joining a network
([`events::WIFI_FAILED`](super::events::WIFI_FAILED)).
The event a screen emits with its result, e.g. the keyboard's text.

A position in a document: section and offset (see
`document::Locator`).
Text, e.g. entered on the keyboard.
A title, e.g. of a book or of what a keyboard asks for.

Set (to `1`) on an answer given while the reader still types
([`Typed::typing`](crate::replies::Typed::typing)).
A web address, e.g. for [`slots::BROWSER`](super::slots::BROWSER).
A word, e.g. to look up.
The sentence being read aloud.
One's own highlights.
Links in a book.
A search hit gone to.
Adds a widget to a list of widgets a setting holds.

Asks to choose one of a few options, e.g. what to do with a file
or whether to delete it (an overlay at the bottom): asked with
[`ask::choice`](crate::ask::choice), answered with a
[`Picked`](crate::ui::choice::Picked). Every plugin's questions
come here, so a screen bound here asks them all another way.

Asks yes or no, e.g. whether to delete a book (a box in the middle
of the screen): asked with [`ask::confirm`](crate::ask::confirm),
answered with a [`Confirmed`](crate::replies::Confirmed), nothing
on *Back* or a tap outside. Every plugin's yes or no questions come
here, so a screen bound here asks them all another way (see

Sizes of the standard UI elements, in pixels: made for the device and

The arrow of semantic icon `icon` ([`icons::BACK`](crate::icons::BACK),

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_button(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, bool, bool)

A button: outlined, or filled when `on`; `focused` (chosen with
buttons) draws a frame around it. Labels of one character (e.g. `+`)
are set larger.

doc:
The row of hints below the screen: a line above it, then what each
button under it does, centred in an equal share of the width, as the
buttons lie. The hint of the button `pressed` is drawn inverted, as a
sign that its press is being worked on.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_card(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_sdk::widgets::look::Frame) -> paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect

Draws a card or frame round `area` (`frame`, as widgets have them:

returns where its parts go: the style's margin in from its edges
(nothing in for [`Frame::None`]). On a dark card, draw in white.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_check(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, bool)
doc:
Draws a box, ticked (`on`) or not, in `rect`; `inverted` on a focused
(black) row. A look of a plugin's own may paint it
([`Painters::check`](super::look::Painters::check)).

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_check_row(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, &str, &str, bool)
doc:
Draws a row of a list where several may be ticked: its box on the
left ([`draw_check`]), `title` beside it, `note` small below where
given. Draw the focus first where it is focused, as for other rows.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_chevron(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, i32, i32, bool, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color)
doc:
An arrow head pointing left or right, centred at `(x, y)` and as tall
as a capital letter of titles. Drawn rather than taken from a font, so
it is centred exactly and needs no special glyph.

An empty screen or list, saying what would be here and how it gets
filled: a large `icon` in gray, a short `title`, and `text` below it,
together a little above the middle of `area`. The icon is left out
where there is not room for all of it, the text shortened last.

Draws the focus of the row or item in `rect` (see [`focus_rect`]):

way, so it looks the same everywhere.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_header(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, core::option::Option<&str>)
doc: A black header bar with a title and an optional right-aligned note.

Draws a section's heading in `rect`: small and gray, low in its room,
so it reads as belonging to the entries below; between the margins, a
long one shortened with "…" as the rows' titles are.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_icon(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &str, f32, f32, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color) -> f32
doc:
Draws icon `name` ([`icons`](crate::icons)) `size` pixels high,
vertically centred in `area`, starting at `x`; returns its width, 0 if
there is no icon font or no such icon.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_icon_at(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &str, f32, (i32, i32), paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color) -> bool
doc:
Draws icon `name` `size` pixels high with its ink centred at
`(x, y)`; `false`, drawing nothing, where it has no drawing.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_icon_button(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, bool, bool) -> paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color
pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_image(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &dyn paperpaw_platform::storage::Storage, &paperpaw_document::ImageRef, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect)
doc:
Draws a decoded image (e.g. a book's cover or an illustration), gray
or in colour, scaled into `area`: each screen row reads one source row
from storage, and columns are averaged when the image is reduced.
Colour shows as colour on colour screens, as gray elsewhere. Where the
frame has few grays, an opaque picture is diffused into them
([`Atkinson`](paperpaw_graphics::diffuse::Atkinson)) from its first
row on, so that each band and each part drawn again shows the same
pixels. A band goes on where the band above left it; a part drawn
again reads its rows above the clip for that, but does not draw them.
Elsewhere only the rows inside the clip are read.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_image_over(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &dyn paperpaw_platform::storage::Storage, &paperpaw_document::ImageRef, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, u8)
doc:
Draws a decoded image over what is drawn in `area`, as
[`draw_image`]: a picture with transparency
([`image::picture_with_alpha`](crate::image::picture_with_alpha))
shows what is below through its clear parts, blended at its edges and
dithered as pictures are; `opacity` (0 to 255) lets what is below show
through all of it, e.g. a picture over the page read. Any screen,
widget or overlay may draw so; rows are read and blended one at a
time, so little memory is taken.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_label(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::FontHandle<'_>, f32, f32, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color) -> f32
doc:
Draws `text` vertically centred in `area`, starting at `x`; text
longer than the rest of the area is shortened with "…", so a label
never runs into what is next to it.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_lines_note(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines, bool, &str)
doc: The note of a number's row below its [`RowLines`].

Draws wrapped, centred message text in `area` ([`message_height`]
high holds all of it).

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_note(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, &str)
doc: Draws the note of a noted row below its [`title_area`].

A note at the bottom of a screen (what a tap or a hold does there, or
what just happened): a light line above it, then `text` in small gray
letters, wrapped on as many lines as `area` holds (the last one
shortened if need be; [`note_line_height`] holds all of it).

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_noted_row(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, &str, &str, &str)

Draws a row with `title` and `value` on its first line and `note` in
small text below, wrapped to [`NOTE_LINES`] lines and shortened with

so a description never needs a tap that would change a setting.
Without a note, the row looks like [`draw_value_row`].

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_number(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, &str, &str, core::option::Option<bool>)
doc:
A number on a light row: its title, then `[−] value [+]` exactly as in
menus, with `room` for the value (see [`stepper`]); `focus` frames the
`−` (`Some(false)`) or the `+` (`Some(true)`).

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_number_lines(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines, &str, &str, &str, core::option::Option<bool>)
doc:
[`draw_number`] on [`RowLines`]: the `−` value `+` below the title
where they are stacked.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_number_note(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, &str)
doc:
Draws the note of a noted row of a number, below its
[`number_title_area`].

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_progress(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, u16, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color)
doc:
Draws a progress bar in `area`, `permille` thousandths done (more than
1000 counts as all): an outline in `ink` with the style's corners,
filled inside it as far as it has come. The fill follows the track's
rounded ends at every value, a sliver at the start or all of it, so no
pixel of it lies outside the track.

Draws `qr` as large as fits in `area`, centred, each module a whole
number of pixels, with the four modules of white around it scanners
expect; returns where it went with that white, or `None` (nothing
drawn) if it does not fit.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_row_icon(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, u16, core::option::Option<&str>, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color) -> paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect
doc:
Draws a list row's icon at the margin, centred on the row's first
line (`rect`), and returns the rest of the row for its label: the
label starts where it would after any icon, so rows line up.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_separator(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, u16)
doc:
Draws the line below the row in `rect` as the style's separators
are: `indent` is where the row's text starts after the margin (e.g.
right of an icon), where faint lines start.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_setting_row(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines, bool, &str, &str, &str)

A setting's row with a value: `title` and `value` on [`RowLines`]
(side by side, or the value below at the right), `note` below them.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_stepper(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, &str, &str, &str, bool)

A focused number: title, then `[−] value [+]`, with `room` for the

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_stepper_lines(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines, &str, &str, &str, bool)

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_switch_lines(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines, bool, &str, &str, bool)

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::draw_value_row(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, bool, &str, &str)

screen: its buttons as in a row made with [`UiStyle::touch_row`], the
room of such a row toward the content, and toward the edge the margin
the screen's sides have, so the buttons keep it from every edge.

the screen it lies along, so that its buttons, centred in it, keep the
side margin from that edge as well.

What opens the keyboard for a text field titled `title` with `value`
in it; what is typed comes back as `reply` ([`ask::text`](crate::ask::text)).

`title` and `text` in their full sizes, without its icon (which it

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::fill(&mut paperpaw_graphics::canvas::Canvas<'_>, paperpaw_platform::geometry::Rect, paperpaw_platform::pixel::Color)

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::fit_pair(&paperpaw_sdk::FontHandle<'_>, f32, &str, &str, f32, f32) -> (alloc::string::String, alloc::string::String, f32)

A title and a value side by side in `width` pixels: both as they are
if they fit, else shortened with "…". The title says what the row is,
so it keeps up to 60 % of the width; the value gets the rest. Returns
the texts and the value's width.

Where the focus of a row or an item in `rect` is drawn: a little in
from the sides, so it sits within the screen's margins as a rounded
bar, and off the lines between rows.

Whether icon `name` has a drawing here (see [`draw_icon`]), e.g. a
semantic icon a theme gave one.
Whether icons can be drawn (an icon font is there).

The height of a section's heading in a list (see [`Rows`]): small
text with a little room above it.

Where icon `name`'s ink begins and ends across at `size`, from where it
is drawn (see [`FontHandle::ink_across`]); `None` without a drawing.

The room icons take at the start of list rows (icon and gap), or 0
without an icon font or when `any` row has none.
The width of icon `name` at `size` pixels, 0 if it cannot be drawn.

How far a navigation action moves a focus: one back for up, left and
previous, one on for down, right and next, `page` for the next page
and back for the previous one; `None` for any other action. Screens
with a [`ListView`] use [`ListView::navigate`].

The height [`draw_message`] needs for all of `text` in an area
`width` wide.

The value after one step of the setting: a switch toggles, a number
moves by `step` within its range, a choice or language moves to the
next (or previous) option. `None` for text.

The height [`draw_note_line`] needs for all of `text` in an area
`width` wide: its light line and the lines of the text.

The height of a noted row `width` wide with `title`, `value` and
`note` (as [`draw_noted_row`] draws it): a noted row
([`UiStyle::noted_row`]), taller where the title takes more lines
beside the value; without a note, [`value_row_height`].

The widest value the numbers among `specs` show, from their least to
their greatest, with their units (and the mark of a value set for a
scope): the room of their steppers (see [`stepper`]) where they are
listed above each other.

The part of a noted row of a number that holds its title and its
`−` and `+`: as [`title_area`], on touch screens as much higher as the
buttons grow to a fingertip ([`UiStyle::touch_row`]); the note goes
below it ([`draw_number_note`]).

Whether choosing the setting opens another screen (its own editor, or
a list to choose from): its row shows a `›`.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::row_lines(&paperpaw_sdk::Env<'_>, &paperpaw_sdk::ui::UiStyle, &paperpaw_sdk::SettingSpec, u16, &str, u32, bool) -> paperpaw_sdk::ui::RowLines

`row` high (`room` for a number's value, see [`number_room`]; `noted`
rows or not): its title and its control side by side, or the control

of rows `row` high: as [`setting_row`], and a title's line more where
the title does not fit beside its control (see [`row_lines`], which
tells both).

What choosing a setting (confirm or a tap) opens, the same on every
screen that lists settings: its editor ([`SettingExtra::editor`](crate::SettingExtra::editor)),
the keyboard for text (a secret entered afresh), the values of a
choice of more than two on the screen of slot
[`CHOOSE_VALUE`](crate::builtin::slots::CHOOSE_VALUE). `None` where
the screen changes it itself: a switch, a number, a choice of two
(see [`next_value`]), or a choice where no screen fills that slot.

`noted` ones ([`UiStyle::noted_row`]) or not: a number's row, which
holds its − and +, grows on touch screens with its buttons
([`UiStyle::touch_row`]; in a noted row its first line,
[`number_title_area`]), the others stay as they are.
The value of a setting for display, with its unit.

signature: pub fn paperpaw_sdk::ui::step_focus(usize, isize, usize) -> usize
doc:
The focus `delta` steps on from `focus` among `len` things: one step
past either end goes round to the other (quicker with few buttons),
larger steps (a page, a row of keys) stop at the end. For screens that
move a focus of their own, as [`ListView`] does.

The − and + buttons of a number row, with room for `room` between
them (at least for "000 %"): the value, or the widest of the
numbers in rows above each other (see [`number_room`]), so their
buttons line up.

Where a stepper's title and its `−` value `+` go in a row `width`
wide and `row` high, at the top left (move them with
[`RowLines::at`]): side by side where the whole title fits beside
them, else the title above, on as many lines as it needs, and the

Display, controls, language and the system.
Room between the others.
Settings whose plugin names no registered group.
One's own: notes, to-dos, pictures.
Book text: font size, spacing, hyphenation, …
Clocks, the date, calendars.
Words and texts: quotes, highlights, vocabulary.
From outside: news, weather.

Its name, translated: the widget's, or the action's.
